name: CoreWeave
founded: 2017 (as Atlantic Crypto; cloud platform 2020; IPO March 2025)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: CoreWeave is the neocloud proxy — the fastest cloud in history to $5B annual revenue (FY2025, +168%), with active power surpassing 1 GW across 49 data centers, 3.5+ GW contracted, and a $99.4B backlog (+284% year over year) after Meta expanded to $21B and OpenAI to ~$22.4B — funded by a GPU-collateralized debt ladder (~$24.9B total) whose cost has fallen from ~15% (2023) to investment-grade SOFR+225bps (the $8.5B DDTL 4.0, rated A3/A-low, March 2026). BACKGROUND: Founded 2017 as Atlantic Crypto; pivoted from mining to GPU cloud in 2020; IPO March 2025 at $40, peaked ~$187, trading ~$91 (August 2026). SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX rated it the industry's sole Platinum GPU cloud, twice. FY2025 net loss $1.17B with Microsoft ~67% of revenue; the $9B Core Scientific acquisition — its main play to own rather than lease power — was voted down by CORZ shareholders in October 2025. Q2 2026 results land August 11.
ecosystemRole: We assess CoreWeave as the demand-side test case for whether contracted AI backlog can carry leveraged infrastructure — the public numbers every private neocloud gets measured against, and a GW-scale power procurer whose posture (leased shells, third-party developers, GPU-backed debt) contrasts instructively with hyperscaler self-build. Basis: 850 MW→1 GW+ active power disclosed quarterly, a Q3 2025 guidance cut caused by a single third-party developer running late (the leased model's fragility made visible), and the failed CORZ deal leaving power verticalization incomplete. For power/BESS vendors, CoreWeave-class buyers move faster than hyperscalers but bring weaker balance sheets — the Vertiv/Switch/Dell consortium that delivered its first GB300 deployment shows the vendor stack it pulls.

productsAndServices.name: GPU cloud platform (the Essential Cloud for AI)
productsAndServices.description: Rack-scale NVIDIA fleet: GB300/GB200 NVL72, B200, H200/H100, plus first-cloud milestones — first GB200 NVL72 general availability, first GB300 NVL72 deployment (July 2025, with Dell/Switch/Vertiv), industry-first Vera Rubin NVL72 bring-up (June 2026: 72 Rubin GPUs + 36 Vera CPUs, 260 TB/s NVLink-6, software-defined liquid cooling with per-rack programmable valve control). Up to 130 kW rack power with liquid cooling; Quantum-2 InfiniBand at 3,200 Gbps; MLPerf records including GPT-3 trained in under 11 minutes.
productsAndServices.positioning: SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX: the only Platinum-tier GPU cloud (AWS/Google/Lambda rated Bronze in the same system) — operational quality, not price, is the differentiator. 9 of the top 10 AI labs are customers.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Multi-year committed contracts (98% of FY2025 revenue); Flex Reservations and Spot for the remainder.
targetSegments: Enterprises entering AI (Jane Street $6B; IBM, Cohere, Mistral)
US federal (FedRAMP pursuit, DOE Genesis Mission, Leidos)
productsAndServices.roadmap: NVIDIA partnership (January 2026, with a $2B equity investment at $87.20) targets >5 GW of AI factories by 2030; company plans >8 GW active power by 2030.

productsAndServices.name: Data-center footprint & power pipeline
productsAndServices.description: 49 active data centers (Q1 2026), 1 GW+ active / 3.5+ GW contracted power. Named projects: Lancaster PA (>$6B, 100→300 MW), Kenilworth NJ (250 MW), Project Horizon West Texas with Poolside (2 GW campus; CoreWeave anchor for 250 MW + 500 MW option, delivering 40,000+ GB300 GPUs), UK (£2.5B), Sweden (renewable-powered with Conapto), Indonesia (three sites, 360 MW contracted, online 2028 — first APAC, CoreWeave-owned).
productsAndServices.positioning: Heavily leased with third-party developers — the Q3 2025 guidance cut from one developer's delay quantified the model's execution exposure; the failed Core Scientific acquisition (~1.3 GW) was the attempted fix.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Lease and build-to-suit agreements; increasing self-operation (Indonesia).
productsAndServices.roadmap: >8 GW active by 2030 target implies ~8x growth in four years — the power pipeline is the product.

productsAndServices.name: Software & services stack (Mission Control, W&B, SUNK)
productsAndServices.description: CoreWeave Mission Control (node/rack/fleet lifecycle and observability — the operational moat behind the ClusterMAX rating), SUNK (Slurm on Kubernetes), AI Object Storage with GPU-local caching, Weights & Biases (acquired ~$1.7B, 2025 — Models, Weave, Inference), OpenPipe (RL), Monolith AI, Marimo, Ventures arm.
productsAndServices.positioning: The software layer converts commodity GPU rental into a managed platform — the argument against the 'no moat' short thesis.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Bundled with capacity contracts; W&B as standalone SaaS.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Agentic tooling (Sandboxes, ARIA research agent) extends the platform play.

recentDevelopments.headline: Core Scientific shareholders voted down the $9B all-stock merger; agreement terminated the same day
recentDevelopments.read: A public-market repudiation of CRWV stock as acquisition currency — and the failure of the main plan to internalize ~1.3 GW of power. CoreWeave remains a tenant on much of its capacity.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess the backlog is real but its equity value hinges on renewal economics and depreciation truth, not the headline number. Basis: $99.4B RPO at ~5-year weighted duration against a 6-year GPU useful-life assumption that shorts (Kerrisdale, Chanos) argue should be 3-4.75 years — a change that would roughly double D&A and erase margins; observed 50-70% rental-rate declines on prior-generation GPUs are the empirical anchor for the bear case.

(High confidence) We assess the debt market has progressively validated the model even as the equity market punishes it. Basis: the coupon trajectory from ~15% (DDTL 1.0, 2023) to investment-grade SOFR+225bps (DDTL 4.0, 2026) is a three-year repricing of GPU-collateral risk by sophisticated lenders — while the stock sold off after four of five earnings prints despite consistent revenue beats.

(High confidence) We assess customer concentration is improving but still defining. Basis: Microsoft ~67% of FY2025 revenue (down from 62%+77% top-two in FY2024), with Meta ($21B), OpenAI (~$22.4B), Anthropic, and Jane Street diversifying the book — but Microsoft declining a ~$12B expansion and routing capacity to Nebius shows the anchor tenant actively cultivating alternatives.

(Moderate confidence) We assess power-ownership incompleteness is the structural weakness the CORZ failure locked in. Basis: heavy lease dependence (~$3.5B lease liabilities), the Q3 2025 developer-delay guidance cut, and the terminated merger that would have brought ~1.3 GW in-house; the Indonesia owned-sites pivot and Project Horizon anchor role are partial substitutes, not replacements.

(Moderate confidence) We assess interest burden is the nearest-term constraint on economics. Basis: FY2025 interest expense $1.23B on $5.13B revenue (~24%), total debt ~$24.9B against ~$4.8B equity; falling coupons help, but the model requires backlog conversion to outrun debt service through the 2026 refinancing tower (~$4.2B due).

relationships.note: The dominant customer — 67% of FY2025 revenue.
relationships.context: Microsoft was 67% of CoreWeave's FY2025 revenue (up from 62% in 2024), with no other customer above 10% — the single biggest commercial fact about the company, and the concentration that makes every diversification win (Meta, Jane Street, HRT) strategically loaded.

relationships.note: ~$22.4B of cumulative contracts — and a $350M equity investor.
relationships.context: The March 2025 master agreement (up to $11.9B, with OpenAI taking $350M of CoreWeave equity) expanded by up to $4B (May 2025) and $6.5B (September 2025, through May 2031) to ~$22.4B cumulative — delivered in part through the Core Scientific Denton campus (16,000+ GPUs deployed by January 2026).

relationships.note: ~$21B expanded agreement through December 2032 for dedicated inference capacity.
relationships.context: September 2025's ~$14.2B agreement expanded to ~$21B in April 2026 — dedicated multi-site capacity for Meta inference including early Vera Rubin deployments, with the ~$19B backlog used as collateral support in the March 2026 $8.5B SPV facility.

relationships.note: Supplier, IPO anchor investor, and $6.3B capacity backstop — customer of last resort through 2032.
relationships.context: Three-sided: CoreWeave is serially first-to-market with NVIDIA platforms (GB200 GA, first GB300 NVL72, early Vera Rubin); NVIDIA anchored the IPO with a $250M order and reportedly provided ~$2B of further support (January 2026, structure unverified); and a September 2025 order form obliges NVIDIA to purchase unsold capacity up to $6.3B through April 2032 — the backstop that de-risks the entire model.

relationships.note: ~590 MW of contracted HPC load across six sites (~$10.2B) — the $9B acquisition was voted down October 2025.
relationships.context: CoreWeave's largest landlord: ~590 MW of contracted critical IT across six Core Scientific sites (~$10.2B over 12-year terms, including the $1.2B Denton expansion). The all-stock acquisition agreed July 2025 was rejected by Core Scientific shareholders on October 30, 2025 and terminated the same day; the commercial partnership continues, with delivery slipping to early 2027 on supply-chain constraints.

relationships.note: 400 MW of ~15-year leases at Polaris Forge 1 (~$11B contracted).
relationships.context: Three leases at Ellendale, ND: 250 MW (~$7B, June 2025) plus 150 MW (August 2025) — ~$11B of contracted revenue, campus scalable to ~1 GW. The March 2026 restructuring assigned leases to a CoreWeave SPV with a springing guaranty and $50M letter of credit — credit engineering alongside the 2026 refinancing.

relationships.note: Host of both world-first NVIDIA bring-ups — GB200 (Nov 2024) and GB300 NVL72 (Jul 2025).
relationships.context: CoreWeave executed the industry-first GB200 NVL72 bring-up and the world-first GB300 NVL72 bring-up (on Dell rack-scale systems) inside Switch's EVO AI Factories — two NVIDIA generations launched first on Switch floors, with CoreWeave as the operating tenant.

relationships.note: Turner-Wohlsen JV builds the $6B Lancaster, PA dedicated campus.
relationships.context: The Turner-Wohlsen JV delivers CoreWeave's up-to-$6B Lancaster, PA site (100 MW initial, scalable to 300 MW; co-developed by Chirisa Technology Parks and Machine Investment Group) — neocloud capital buying hyperscaler-tier construction.

relationships.note: Fuel cells power the Chirisa-hosted Volo, IL site — commissioned Q3 2025.
relationships.context: Bloom's solid-oxide fuel cells supply on-site power at the Volo, Illinois data center hosting CoreWeave (14 MW, partnership announced 2024, commissioned Q3 2025) — the only named CoreWeave-specific generation vendor; elsewhere power procurement sits with its landlords.

relationships.note: Reuters-reported capacity supply to Google Cloud — never company-confirmed.
relationships.context: June 2025 Reuters reporting had CoreWeave supplying compute capacity to Google Cloud (in turn serving OpenAI); neither company has announced it. Held as reported-only.
